final_answer:
Studies have shown that there are several reasons why women earn less than men. These include:

1. Gender-based discrimination: Women are often paid less than men for the same job, even when they have similar qualifications and experience.
2. Unconscious bias: Both men and women may unconsciously favor men over women in hiring and promotions.
3. Caregiving responsibilities: Women are more likely to take time off work to care for children or elderly relatives, which can affect their career advancement.
4. Occupational segregation: Women are more likely to work in lower-paying fields such as education, healthcare, and social work, while men are more likely to work in higher-paying fields such as engineering and finance.

Sources:

1. National Women's Law Center. (2021). The Gender Pay Gap. Retrieved from <https://nwlc.org/resource/the-gender-pay-gap/>
2. Catalyst. (2021). The Bias That Threatens Your Diversity and Inclusion Efforts. Retrieved from <https://www.catalyst.org/research/bias-threatens-diversity-and-inclusion-efforts/>
3. Peterson, K. (2019). Why Women Don't Ask: The Cost of Gender Socialization. Oxford University Press.
4. U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics. (2021). Highlights of women's earnings in 2020. Retrieved from <https://www.bls.gov/opub/reports/womens-earnings/2020/home.htm>
